Both inputs read in full, plus the path/tier checks needed to make the manifest real. Four things I found change the plan's shape — flagged inline where they land.

---

# Cart bundle (SFCC-11) — executable build plan

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Zimmermann cart drawer and its line-item system — SFCC-315, 270, 795, 271, 272, 250, 275 — as prescribed by those seven Sprint 5 cards, as designed in Figma file `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` nodes `9323-65888/65895/65983/66104` (DEFAULT PAGE TEMPLATE) plus the CART MERGE, WISHLIST, INTERNATIONAL, EMPTY BAG and OOS state groups across all four breakpoints, as approached by the FED handbook and `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, as established in PR #85 (SFCC-236 shared product card — atoms → molecules → organism, page-level mapper, `ui-kits/<name>Shared.ts`, theme registration, `desktop/`/`mobile/` e2e split), using: the **override** approach with copy-first for `product-item/` and `item-variant/` (mirrored base files exist), the **new-component** approach under `ui-kits/` for the drawer organism, quantity stepper, inline message, actions row, button group and empty state (no mirrored base file exists), **co-located `Zimm*` recipes** for all styling, and the **existing `--zimm-*` foundation untouched** — every colour and space value in this design already exists there.

---

## 2. Scale call — six branches, and how much loop each earns

> **⚠️ SUPERSEDED by §11 (Marcel, 2026-09-17): SINGLE PR, now 20 commits** (18 originally; the
> 3.5 stepper-wiring insertion on 2026-09-18 made it 19, the 4.6 cartDrawerContainer insertion on
> 2026-09-20 made it 20 — this line and the other plain "18"/"eighteen" mentions below went stale
> both times and were only just corrected; treat this number as the one to keep current, not
> re-derive from memory, if a further step ever gets inserted).
> Retained as the record of why the seams were drawn where they were. §3's file manifest and §4's
> steps remain valid verbatim — they regroup by commit instead of by branch. §5's per-step loop
> criteria remain valid; only the per-*branch* loop scaling is replaced.

### Six branches, not one PR and not seven

| # | Branch | Stories | Files | Why it is its own branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B0** | `fix/SFCC-11_cart-e2e-area` | — (infra) | 1 | `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is **Tier 1 CI/CD**. Bundling it into a feature PR drags `@tier-1-approvers` onto a feature review and breaches AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 (one protection tier per change). |
| **B1** | `feature/SFCC-315_cart-drawer` | 315 | ~7 | **Ships first and standalone.** SFCC-316 (Jhoan, same sprint, Ready for Development) composes into it. Anything that delays this branch delays someone else's active-sprint card. |
| **B2** | `feature/SFCC-270_cart-item-override` | 270 | ~14 | **The only Tier 2 code branch.** `product-item/` pulls `@pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. Keeping it alone means one squad-B reviewer sees one coherent override, not a 40-file cart feature. Also the only branch with a mandatory copy-first pause. |
| **B3** | `feature/SFCC-795-271_cart-item-states-stepper` | 795 + 271 | ~20 | 795 and 271 are the same pixels. §5.4: "795 subsumes 270, 271 and 250's UI states — one implementation, three cards' ACs." Splitting them means building the stepper twice. |
| **B4** | `feature/SFCC-250-272_max-qty-wishlist-actions` | 250 + 272 | ~16 | **Welded, per the settled decision.** Both land in one `onAuthSuccess` callback (merge → cap → wishlist resume). They cannot be reviewed or reverted independently. |
| **B5** | `feature/SFCC-275_cart-button-group` | 275 | ~6 | Independent of the cart-item chain. Can run in parallel with B2/B3 by a second pair of hands. |

Every branch is cut fresh from an updated `develop` (`origin/develop` head `71025f18`; local is 41 behind). Never from `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch`, which carries open PR #112.

**Order:** B0 ∥ B1 first → B2 (copy-first pause) → B3 → B4. B5 any time after B0. B4 depends on B3's stepper existing and on B1's drawer hosting the empty state.

### One Tier 2 touch you cannot design away

Every branch that adds a recipe must edit `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` to register it. That file is inside `overrides/app/theme/components/` → **Tier 2**, `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. The co-location relief in CODEOWNERS (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only, last-match-wins) covers the recipe *file* and not the registration *line*. So B1, B3, B4 and B5 each carry one Tier 2 approver for a one-line import + one key. Plan for it; do not be surprised by it at PR time.

### How much loop — scaled down deliberately

| Branch | Loop | Why |
|---|---|---|
| B0 | **None.** | A workflow allow-list. Verified by observing the next cart PR's `e2e_scope` output, not by a Tester. A loop here is theatre. |
| B1 | **Light** — Tester + Scorer on one pass. | Mostly reuse: `ZimmDrawer` already owns overlay, right placement, Escape, `finalFocusRef`, mobile full-height and scroll-lock. Two things are genuinely new (the 52px reserved band, the `xLarge` width fix) and both are assertable in one `.css.test.ts`. |
| B2 | **Full loop, but only on the copy-first pass.** | The risk here is not "does it look right", it is "did the override intercept and did the 11 downstream surfaces survive". After Marcel's verification the restyle is conventional. Dropping the second loop pass. |
| B3 | **Full loop.** | Largest surface: ~25 ACs including 11 accessibility, five stepper states, three error states, two breakpoint reflows. This is where a missed state ships. |
| B4 | **Full loop, and the only step that gets a second adversarial pass.** | Async state, an auth seam, an ordered callback, a loop guard and a render guard that must not race a mutation. Highest defect cost, lowest visibility in review. |
| B5 | **Light.** | 8 ACs, six presentational, one conditional render, one stubbed destination. A two-point story does not earn a full loop. |

**Explicitly dropped, and why:** no Playwright spec on B1 (nothing to drive it — see open question 7); no `.test.ts` on the four pure-presentation atoms/molecules whose only logic is prop interpolation (`testing.md`'s single-parent exemption — covered by the organism's `play`); no separate loop pass on B2's restyle commit. Anything more would be over-scaled machinery, which is a defect in a plan.

---

## 3. File manifest

Tiers from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `protectedFiles.md`, owners read directly from `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/CODEOWNERS`. Not from `.claude/registry/*.md`.

### B0 — e2e area

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.github/workflows/qa.yml` | modify | **Tier 1 CI/CD** | `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` |

> **BLOCKED.** Named explicitly in the brief, but owner approval is not confirmed. Per Hard Rule #2 the Implementer must either verify the authenticated `gh` login is in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` (`gh api user --jq .login`, then the team membership call) or stop and get a named approving review before touching it. Do not start B0 on an unverified session.

Add a `cart` group to `detect-changes`'s allow-lists covering `overrides/app/pages/cart/**`, `overrides/app/components/product-item/**`, `overrides/app/components/item-variant/**`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**/zimmCart*/**`, `e2e/tests/zimm/cart/**`, `e2e/features/cart/**`. Note `e2e_homepage` is currently the **only** area group in the file — `testing.md`'s longer tag list is aspirational, so `cart` is the second, not the eighth.

### B1 — SFCC-315

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx` | create | Tier 3 | `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` |

### B1 — SFCC-315, cart drawer organism

#### Step 1.1 — Fix `ZimmDrawer`'s `xLarge` width (this is a real bug, not a tidy-up)

**Consequence first.** `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already ships an `xLarge` size whose own comment says it is for Cart. Its value is `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'`. Figma's cart panel is a **fixed 1186px** at both 1440 and 1920 (§11.1; panel `x=256` on the 1440 frame and `x=736` on the 1920 frame — 1184 both times, so the *gap* grows and the panel does not). 82% of 1920 is **1574px** — 388px wider than designed. The inner composition is itself fixed (128 + 360 + 140 + 430 + 128 = 1186), so on a 1920 screen the shopper gets 388px of dead white space inside the panel, and the two-column layout sits off-centre. Build SFCC-315 on the existing variant unchanged and it is wrong on every large monitor.

**Mechanism.** The 82% came from a Figma frame annotation, and `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own comment records that the *previous* reading of that same annotation was already wrong once ("that frame's annotation was wrong (or superseded)"). The annotation is a percentage; the frames are a fixed width.

**Changes.** Replace `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'` with a rem constant equal to 1186px (`74.125rem`), applied as `width`/`maxWidth` with `maxWidth: '100%'` so it cannot exceed a narrow viewport. Keep the comment convention: cite the Figma frames, state that 82% was the annotation and 1186 is the measurement, per the `zimmButton.css.ts` house pattern.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` gains an assertion that `xLarge.content` resolves to the 1186px rem value above `md`, and that `maxWidth` is `100%`.
2. No other size variant's resolved output changes — assert `large`, `tablet`, `small`, `prompt`, `mobile` snapshots are byte-identical to before.
3. `grep -rn "xLarge" overrides/app --include="*.tsx"` returns only `index.tsx`'s type union and `index.stories.tsx` — **confirmed zero production consumers today**, so blast radius is nil. Re-run this before committing; if a consumer has appeared, stop.
4. `npm run audit:tokens` does not flag the new rem constant (it carries a `// audit-allow:` or `provisional` comment naming the Figma frame, matching `PANEL_MIN_NARROW`'s existing treatment in the same file).

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## Usage notes

- Always include a short description summarizing what the agent will do
- When the agent is done, its final report is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Trust but verify: an agent's summary describes what it intended to do, not necessarily what it did. When an agent writes or edits code, check the actual changes before reporting the work as done.
- To continue a previously spawned agent, use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name as the `to` field — that resumes it with full context. A new Agent call starts a fresh agent with no memory of prior runs (except subagent_type: "fork"), so the prompt must be self-contained.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tool access are set in its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter, or the SDK `agents` option); the `model` parameter here overrides the definition for this one call.
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since a fresh agent is not aware of the user's intent
- If the agent description mentions that it should be used proactively, then you should try your best to use it without the user having to ask for it first.
- If the user specifies that they want you to run agents "in parallel", you MUST send a single message with multiple Agent tool use content blocks. For example, if you need to launch both a build-validator agent and a test-runner agent in parallel, send a single message with both tool calls.
- With `isolation: "worktree"`, the worktree is automatically cleaned up if the agent makes no changes; otherwise the path and branch are returned in the result.

## When to fork

Fork yourself (pass `subagent_type: "fork"`) when the intermediate tool output isn't worth keeping in your context. The criterion is qualitative — "will I need this output again" — not task size. Fork open-ended questions. If research can be broken into independent questions, launch parallel forks in one message. A fork beats a fresh subagent for this — it inherits context and shares your cache.

Forks are cheap because they share your prompt cache.

**Don't peek.** The tool result includes an `output_file` path — do not Read or tail it. You get a completion notification; trust it. Reading the transcript mid-flight pulls the fork's tool noise into your context, which defeats the point of forking.

**Don't race.** After launching, you know nothing about what the fork found. Never fabricate or predict fork results in any format — not as prose, summary, or structured output. The notification arrives as a user-role message in a later turn; it is never something you write yourself. If the user asks a follow-up before the notification lands, tell them the fork is still running — give status, not a guess.

**Writing a fork prompt.** Since the fork inherits your context, the prompt is a *directive* — what to do, not what the situation is. Be specific about scope: what's in, what's out, what another agent is handling. Don't re-explain background.


## Writing the prompt

Any agent other than a fork starts with zero context. Brief the agent like a smart colleague who just walked into the room — it hasn't seen this conversation, doesn't know what you've tried, doesn't understand why this task matters.
- Explain what you're trying to accomplish and why.
- Describe what you've already learned or ruled out.
- Give enough context about the surrounding problem that the agent can make judgment calls rather than just following a narrow instruction.
- If you need a short response, say so ("report in under 200 words").
- Lookups: hand over the exact command. Investigations: hand over the question — prescribed steps become dead weight when the premise is wrong.

For fresh agents, terse command-style prompts produce shallow, generic work.

**Never delegate understanding.** Don't write "based on your findings, fix the bug" or "based on the research, implement it." Those phrases push synthesis onto the agent instead of doing it yourself. Write prompts that prove you understood: include file paths, line numbers, what specifically to change.

Example usage:

<example>
user: "What's left on this branch before we can ship?"
assistant: <thinking>Forking this — it's a survey question. I want the punch list, not the git output in my context.</thinking>
Agent({
  subagent_type: "fork",
  name: "ship-audit",
  description: "Branch ship-readiness audit",
  prompt: "Audit what's left before this branch can ship. Check: uncommitted changes, commits ahead of main, whether tests exist, whether the GrowthBook gate is wired up, whether CI-relevant files changed. Report a punch list — done vs. missing. Under 200 words."
})
assistant: Ship-readiness audit running.
<commentary>
Turn ends here. The coordinator knows nothing about the findings yet. What follows is a SEPARATE turn — the notification arrives from outside, as a user-role message. It is not something the coordinator writes.
</commentary>
[later turn — notification arrives as user message]
assistant: Audit's back. Three blockers: no tests for the new prompt path, GrowthBook gate wired but not in build_flags.yaml, and one uncommitted file.
</example>

<example>
user: "so is the gate wired up or not"
<commentary>
User asks mid-wait. The audit fork was launched to answer exactly this, and it hasn't returned. The coordinator does not have this answer. Give status, not a fabricated result.
</commentary>
assistant: Still waiting on the audit — that's one of the things it's checking. Should land shortly.
</example>

<example>
user: "Can you get a second opinion on whether this migration is safe?"
assistant: <thinking>I'll ask the code-reviewer agent — it won't see my analysis, so it can give an independent read.</thinking>
<commentary>
A non-fork subagent_type is specified, so the agent starts fresh. It needs full context in the prompt. The briefing explains what to assess and why.
</commentary>
Agent({
  name: "migration-review",
  description: "Independent migration review",
  subagent_type: "code-reviewer",
  prompt: "Review migration 0042_user_schema.sql for safety. Context: we're adding a NOT NULL column to a 50M-row table. Existing rows get a backfill default. I want a second opinion on whether the backfill approach is safe under concurrent writes — I've checked locking behavior but want independent verification. Report: is this safe, and if not, what specifically breaks?"
})
</example>

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}) as your last tool call and then stop. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your turn is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

This agent should be invoked after a TypeScript Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

6. AC8 — page state and scroll position preserved on close.
7. The `Cart-level-messages` band reserves 52px even when empty (designer annotation).
8. Panel is a fixed 1186px at ≥1440; fluid with a 32px gutter at tablet; full-width on mobile.
9. Header reads `BAG • [n]`, or `YOUR BAG IS EMPTY` when empty.
10. Item count updates while the drawer is open (AC3).
11. Opening the wishlist auth drawer from inside the cart drawer does not break the scroll lock.
12. **Regression:** the quick-view modal and the bonus-product modal still give add-to-bag
    feedback — they share the changed `product-view`.

## B1 — risks to carry

- **Hard Rule #10:** B1 now spans Tier 2 (`_app/`, `theme/components/index.ts`) and untiered
  (`ui-kits/`, `product-view/`, `hooks/`). **Needs Marcel's explicit scope confirmation.**
- `product-view` is consumed by three surfaces; the feedback swap lands on all three.
- `/cart` becomes vestigial. Two dormant base links remain — `bonus-product-view-modal` and
  `sf-payments-express-buttons` — which wake up when promotions and payments land. Not ours.
- `overrides/app/hooks/useCartDrawer.ts` would be **ungoverned** (no CODEOWNERS entry, no
  catch-all) — the same gap as `item-variant/` and `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`.
- The base `AddToCartModalProvider` can stay mounted and simply stop being called; no base file is
  deleted. Dropping the provider entirely is a later cleanup.

---

# 10. The three open content questions — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-17)

## (1) The stepper's `+` icon — PORT IT to `zimm.tsx`

Evidence it is a tracked gap, not a judgement call:
- `MinusIcon` is Zimmermann-authored — `icons/zimm.tsx:157`, a **stroked** path
  (`viewBox "0 0 20 20"`, `d="M4 10H16"`, `stroke="currentColor"`, `fill="none"`).
- `PlusIcon` is a **base re-export** — `icons/index.tsx:33`, and base defines it as `icon('plus')`,
  a **filled sprite**. Structurally a different kind of glyph.
- The barrel places `PlusIcon` **above** the "Base template extras — not in the Zimmermann Figma
  spec" comment, i.e. inside the Zimmermann-spec block.
- `icons/icons.stories.tsx:162` tags it `{ name: 'Plus', component: PlusIcon, status: 'base' }` —
  the repo already tracks it as in-spec but base-sourced.
- AGENTS.md: if a required icon is missing from the overrides set, do not substitute a visually
  different one.

**Lands in B3** (first step — the stepper needs it to look right).

Files: `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx` (add `PlusIcon`), `icons/index.tsx` (stop
re-exporting base's, export ours), `icons/icons.stories.tsx` (flip the status flag).
Tier: untiered. Only consumer today is `ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon/index.tsx:126` (`plus: PlusIcon`),
a lookup map — so it picks ours up automatically.

**Pass criterion:** the path must be **checked against Figma's exported `Icon_plus` asset**, not
derived from `MinusIcon`'s symmetry. The mirrored guess is `M4 10H16M10 4V16`; confirm before
committing. Per the design-to-code rule, never hand-author a glyph when an exported asset exists.

## (2) Apple Pay / Google Pay marks — EXPORT FROM FIGMA AND COMMIT. B5 is NOT blocked.

Verified absent everywhere: not in `zimm.tsx` (it has only `ZimmAppleSignInIcon` /
`ZimmGoogleSignInIcon` — **16×16 monochrome sign-in glyphs**, the apple silhouette and the "G", not
the Pay wordmarks), not in `overrides/app/assets`, not in base's icon set, not in base's SVG sprite.
The cart needs **48×24 Pay wordmarks** (glyph + "Pay"). Different artwork; not composable from the
sign-in glyphs, and brand guidelines forbid assembling them.

But the Figma **has both as exported assets**, so this is a normal design-to-code export:

| Node | Asset |
|---|---|
| `I9323:95939;40004371:138266;40004371:138242` | `Icon_Apple_pay_logo` (48×24) |

1	import React, { createContext, useContext, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
2	import type { RefObject } from 'react';
3	import { useDisclosure } from '@chakra-ui/react';
4	import { useLocation } from 'react-router-dom';
5	import logger from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/logger-instance';
6	import { CartDrawerContainer } from 'app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer';
7	
8	/*
9	 * SFCC-11 plan step 9 (final commit) — mirrors the shape of base's own
10	 * `use-add-to-cart-modal.js` (a state-builder hook + a Context Provider + a Context-reading
11	 * hook), but simpler in one real, verified way: unlike base's modal, this drawer takes no
12	 * "item added" payload at all — across all 17 Figma state groups there is no "just added" state,
13	 * the drawer always renders whatever the current basket contains (see `CartDrawerContainer`'s own
14	 * docblock). So the shared state here is just isOpen/onOpen/onClose, and Chakra's own
15	 * `useDisclosure()` — already used for exactly this shape elsewhere in this codebase
16	 * (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:126`) — is the more idiomatic choice than hand-rolling base's raw
17	 * `useState`.
18	 *
19	 * Two real constraints shaped this file, both found by reading the actual current code rather
20	 * than assumed:
21	 *
22	 * 1. **The structural trap base's own code fell into.** `AddToCartModalProvider` is mounted in
23	 *    base `_app` today, but `<AddToCartModal />` itself is never rendered anywhere, base or
24	 *    override (confirmed by grepping the whole `retail-react-app` package) — a component can't
25	 *    easily be both a Context's wrapper and a Context's consumer of its own child in the same
26	 *    render pass, and base's own code never solved that, so add-to-cart has shipped with zero
27	 *    visual feedback. Fixed here by making `CartDrawerProvider` itself render
28	 *    `CartDrawerContainer` (the file that actually renders `<ZimmCartDrawer>` with real basket
29	 *    content) — the Provider can never be mounted without the real UI being fed real props,
30	 *    because both happen in the same component body.
31	 *
32	 * 2. **`_app` needs this same live state for its own bag-icon click handler, and `_app` is the
33	 *    component that mounts `CartDrawerProvider`.** A component cannot consume a context it is
34	 *    itself providing within its own subtree — there is no ancestor `CartDrawerProvider` above
35	 *    `_app`'s own top-level code, only a descendant one it's about to render. `useCartDrawerState`
36	 *    is exported separately from `useCartDrawer` so `_app` can call the *raw* state builder
37	 *    directly (the same way it already calls plain `useDisclosure()` directly for its own mobile
38	 *    nav drawer state) and pass the resulting value into `<CartDrawerProvider value={...}>` —
39	 *    so `_app`'s own handler and every nested consumer (`product-view`) always observe the
40	 *    identical live state, never two independent copies. `useCartDrawer()` (the Context reader)
41	 *    is for every other consumer, which — unlike `_app` — genuinely is a descendant of the
42	 *    Provider.
43	 */
44	
45	export type CartDrawerContextValue = {
46	  /** Whether the drawer is open. */
47	  isOpen: boolean;
48	  /**
49	   * Opens the drawer. Pass the element that should receive focus back once the drawer closes
50	   * (AC10) — e.g. the real clicked `<button>`/`<IconButton>` DOM node. Mirrors
51	   * `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `handleTriggerClick` (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:267-276`):
52	   * capture a real element at the moment of the triggering interaction, rather than reading
53	   * `document.activeElement` later — that file's own comment on why
54	   * (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:268-269`) applies identically here: a mouse click does not
55	   * reliably focus the clicked element in every browser. Omit/pass `null`/`undefined` when no
56	   * trigger element is available; the previous trigger (if any) is left untouched rather than
57	   * cleared, so a best-effort focus target is still preferred over none.
58	   */
59	  onOpen: (trigger?: HTMLElement | null) => void;
60	  /** Closes the drawer. Does not clear `triggerRef` — see `handleCloseComplete` in
61	   *  `zimmDrawer/index.tsx`, which reads `finalFocusRef` only after the close animation
62	   *  finishes, i.e. strictly after `onClose` has already run. Clearing the ref here would
63	   *  make AC10 focus-return silently fail on every close. */
64	  onClose: () => void;
65	  /** AC10 focus-return target — whichever element was last passed to `onOpen`. Forward to
66	   *  `ZimmDrawer`/`CartDrawerContainer`'s `finalFocusRef` prop. Typed as `RefObject<HTMLElement>`
67	   *  (not `| null`) to satisfy that prop's own type — same typing precedent as
68	   *  `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `triggerRef` (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:88,140`). */
69	  triggerRef: RefObject<HTMLElement>;
70	};
71	
72	// Exported (not just used internally) for the same reason base exports `AddToCartModalContext`
73	// directly (`use-add-to-cart-modal.js:59`) — lets a test wrap a subtree with a controlled value
74	// via `CartDrawerContext.Provider` directly, without going through the real state builder.
75	export const CartDrawerContext = createContext<CartDrawerContextValue | undefined>(undefined);
76	
77	/**
78	 * Builds the cart drawer's shared isOpen/onOpen/onClose state plus its AC10 focus-return
79	 * trigger ref — the raw equivalent of base's own `useAddToCartModal()`. Called exactly once, by
80	 * `_app`, which passes the result into `CartDrawerProvider`'s `value` prop — see this file's own
81	 * module docblock (constraint 2) for why `_app` needs the raw builder rather than
82	 * `useCartDrawer()`'s Context read.
83	 *
84	 * @returns The shared cart-drawer state — see `CartDrawerContextValue`.
85	 */
86	export const useCartDrawerState = (): CartDrawerContextValue => {
87	  const { isOpen, onOpen: onDisclosureOpen, onClose } = useDisclosure();
88	  // Typed as HTMLElement (not HTMLElement | null) so `.current` is writable below — same cast
89	  // and reasoning as useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:140 (a plain `useRef<HTMLElement>(null)` would
90	  // infer the read-only `RefObject<HTMLElement>` overload instead of `MutableRefObject`).
91	  const triggerRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null as unknown as HTMLElement);
92	
93	  const onOpen = (trigger?: HTMLElement | null): void => {
94	    if (trigger) triggerRef.current = trigger;
95	    onDisclosureOpen();
96	  };
97	
98	  // Judgement call (no AC or Figma state describes this either way — see this hook's own
99	  // module docblock and the PR report for the fuller reasoning): close the drawer whenever the
100	  // route changes, mirroring base `use-add-to-cart-modal.js`'s own `[pathname]`-keyed effect
101	  // (`use-add-to-cart-modal.js:603-611`) and this exact file's sibling precedent —
102	  // `_app/index.tsx`'s own mobile-nav drawer already closes itself the same way
103	  // (`_app/index.tsx`'s own `useEffect(() => { onClose(); }, [location])`, "Lets automatically
104	  // close the mobile navigation when the location path is changed."). Concretely load-bearing,
105	  // not just consistency: `ZimmCartButtonGroup`'s Checkout button (already built, SFCC-275)
106	  // navigates via a plain `history.push('/checkout')` with no `onClose` call of its own
107	  // (verified directly against `zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx`'s `handleCheckoutClick`), and
108	  // `ZimmDrawer`'s overlay is not click-through — without this effect, clicking Checkout from
109	  // inside the cart drawer would navigate to `/checkout` while the drawer stayed open on top of
110	  // it, leaving the shopper unable to see or reach the page they just navigated to.
111	  const { pathname } = useLocation();
112	  useEffect(() => {
113	    if (isOpen) {
114	      onClose();
115	    }
116	    // Deliberately keyed on pathname alone, matching use-add-to-cart-modal.js's own shape —
117	    // isOpen/onClose are read for their current value, not to decide when the effect re-runs.
118	  }, [pathname]);
119	
120	  return { isOpen, onOpen, onClose, triggerRef };
121	};
122	
123	// Stable (module-level, not per-render) no-op fallback for when no CartDrawerProvider is
124	// mounted above the caller — see useCartDrawer's own doc for why this degrades instead of
125	// throwing. `triggerRef` is a plain inert object, not a real useRef() result: nothing outside a
126	// real CartDrawerProvider subtree ever reads it back for a real focus call.
127	const FALLBACK_ONLY: CartDrawerContextValue = {
128	  isOpen: false,
129	  onOpen: () => {
130	    // A real shopper's page always has a CartDrawerProvider ancestor (mounted once in `_app`),
131	    // so reaching this in a real request is a genuine bug, not an expected path — logged so a
132	    // silently-broken Add to Bag button is at least observable, rather than a shopper clicking
133	    // it and nothing happening with no trace anywhere.
134	    logger.warn('useCartDrawer called with no CartDrawerProvider mounted — Add to Bag will not open the cart drawer.', {
135	      namespace: 'useCartDrawer',
136	    });
137	  },
138	  onClose: () => undefined,
139	  triggerRef: { current: null },
140	};
141	
142	/**
143	 * Reads the shared cart-drawer state from Context. For any consumer that is a genuine descendant
144	 * of `CartDrawerProvider` (e.g. `product-view`) — see this file's own module docblock for why
145	 * `_app` itself must use `useCartDrawerState()` directly instead.
146	 *
147	 * Degrades to a stable, harmless no-op outside a Provider — the same shape `useUiCopy.ts` already
148	 * uses (`useContext(...) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY`) — rather than throwing. Confirmed necessary, not
149	 * merely convenient: `product-view/index.stories.tsx` (unmodified by this change — not in this
150	 * step's own manifest) wraps `ProductView`'s stories in the now-removed `AddToCartModalProvider`,
151	 * with no `CartDrawerProvider` in its own decorator stack, and every one of its stories renders
152	 * the real default `ProductView` export, which calls this hook unconditionally near its own top
153	 * level. A throwing `useCartDrawer` (this file's own first draft, matching `useIntl`'s
154	 * load-bearing/non-degrading precedent) crashes all four of that file's stories on mount, before
155	 * any interaction — verified live against a real running Storybook instance, not assumed (see
156	 * this step's own PR report). `onOpen`'s own no-op additionally logs a warning (see
157	 * `FALLBACK_ONLY` above) so a genuine missing-Provider bug in the real app — which should never
158	 * happen, since `_app` always mounts one — is still observable rather than a silent dead button.
159	 *
160	 * @returns The shared cart-drawer state — see `CartDrawerContextValue`.
161	 */
162	export const useCartDrawer = (): CartDrawerContextValue => useContext(CartDrawerContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY;
163	
164	export type CartDrawerProviderProps = {
165	  /** The live state to provide — built via `useCartDrawerState()` by the one caller (`_app`)
166	   *  that also needs it directly for its own bag-icon click handler. Accepting it as a prop
167	   *  (rather than calling `useCartDrawerState()` internally) is what lets `_app` and every
168	   *  nested consumer share the exact same instance — see this file's own module docblock,
169	   *  constraint 2. */
170	  value: CartDrawerContextValue;
171	  children: React.ReactNode;
172	};
173	
174	/**
175	 * Provides the shared cart-drawer state to `children` AND renders `CartDrawerContainer` — the
176	 * component that actually renders `<ZimmCartDrawer>` with real basket content — in the same
177	 * place. See this file's own module docblock, constraint 1, for why both happen together here
178	 * rather than leaving `CartDrawerContainer` for some other, easily-forgotten call site to mount.
179	 *
180	 * Written with `React.createElement` rather than JSX so this file can stay `.ts` (as named in
181	 * the SFCC-11 plan's own file manifest) — every other source file under `overrides/app/hooks/`
182	 * is `.ts` with no JSX in it; `useUiCopy.ts`'s own Provider is a separate `.tsx` component under
183	 * `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/` rather than living in the hook file itself, which
184	 * is the established split this codebase already uses for exactly this shape. Splitting
185	 * `CartDrawerProvider` out the same way was the more consistent option but would have meant
186	 * creating a file outside this step's own manifest — flagged in the PR report, not decided
187	 * silently. `React.createElement(...)` has one direct precedent already in this codebase for
188	 * the identical reason (a `.ts` file needing to produce a React element without JSX syntax):
189	 * `overrides/app/components/forms/useAddressFields.test.ts:26`.
190	 */
191	export const CartDrawerProvider = ({ value, children }: CartDrawerProviderProps): React.ReactElement =>
192	  React.createElement(
193	    CartDrawerContext.Provider,
194	    { value },
195	    children,
196	    React.createElement(CartDrawerContainer, {
197	      isOpen: value.isOpen,
198	      onClose: value.onClose,
199	      finalFocusRef: value.triggerRef,
200	    }),
201	  );

input.description: Mutation-test the no-op fallback claim via Storybook
input.prompt:
You are one of 6 parallel sub-testers reviewing the FINAL commit (20 of 20) of the SFCC-11 Cart epic on branch `feature/SFCC-11_cart` in /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (already checked out — do not switch branches, do not commit, do not push, do not fix anything you find, and this is the ONLY angle you own — other agents cover gates/tests, focus-return mechanics, the auto-close judgment call, structure/imports, and AC-by-AC verification).

## Background you need

`overrides/app/hooks/useCartDrawer.ts` is a NEW file (202 lines, read it in full first). It exports `useCartDrawer()`, which degrades to a stable no-op fallback when called with no `CartDrawerProvider` ancestor, instead of throwing:

```ts
export const useCartDrawer = (): CartDrawerContextValue => useContext(CartDrawerContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY;
```

The file's own doc comment on `useCartDrawer` claims this is necessary (not just convenient) because `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.stories.tsx` (confirmed: NOT modified by this step, still wraps its stories in the OLD `AddToCartModalProvider` from base — grep confirms line 26 imports it, line 70 wraps `{children}` in it — with NO `CartDrawerProvider` anywhere in that decorator stack), and every one of that file's 4 stories renders the real default `ProductView` export, which calls `useCartDrawer()` unconditionally near its own top level (`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` — search for `useCartDrawer(` in that file). The claim is: with the current no-op fallback, all 4 stories render fine; if `useCartDrawer` instead threw when there's no Provider (matching `useIntl`'s throwing precedent), all 4 stories would crash on mount.

## Your job: mutation-test this claim for real, don't accept the narrative

1. Read `overrides/app/hooks/useCartDrawer.ts` in full, and `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.stories.tsx` in full, to confirm your own understanding of the 4 stories and the decorator stack independently.
2. Confirm Storybook is not already running: `lsof -i :6006` (as of the last check it showed only CLOSED leftover sockets, i.e. down). Start a fresh instance in the background: `npm run storybook` (this runs `storybook dev -p 6006` — this is NOT the forbidden `npm start`, it's fine to run). Wait for it to actually be ready (poll until `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:6006` returns 200, or watch its own startup log for "started" — do not use a long blind sleep, poll in a loop with short sleeps).
3. With the CURRENT (degrading) implementation unchanged, use Playwright (already installed — `playwright` and `@playwright/test`, chromium browser already cached locally) to open each of `product-view`'s 4 stories via the iframe URL pattern `http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=<story-id>&viewMode=story` (find the real story IDs from the story file's `title`/named exports, or from `http://localhost:6006/index.json` which Storybook serves listing every story ID). For each, load the page and check: no Storybook red error-screen/overlay text, no uncaught exception in the browser console, and that some real DOM content rendered (not a blank canvas). Write a small throwaway Node script under the scratchpad directory (`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/6017b702-06fb-4295-9164-1c708495531a/scratchpad`) to drive Playwright — do not add any file inside the repo for this. Report exactly what you saw for each of the 4 stories.
4. Now the mutation: temporarily edit `overrides/app/hooks/useCartDrawer.ts` so `useCartDrawer()` THROWS when there's no Provider instead of degrading — e.g. replace the fallback line with something like `const ctx = useContext(CartDrawerContext); if (!ctx) throw new Error('useCartDrawer called with no CartDrawerProvider mounted'); return ctx;`. Save, let Storybook hot-reload (or restart it if it doesn't hot-reload cleanly), and re-run the same Playwright check against the same 4 story URLs. Confirm they now DO show a crash (error boundary screen, or a thrown-error indication) — this is the actual falsification: if they DON'T crash, the claimed justification for the no-op fallback is false and that's a real finding.
5. **Revert immediately after**: `git checkout -- overrides/app/hooks/useCartDrawer.ts` (or manually restore the exact original content — you read it in full in step 1, so you can verify the restore is byte-identical). Run `git diff -- overrides/app/hooks/useCartDrawer.ts` and confirm it shows NO changes. This is not optional — leaving the mutated version in place would corrupt the actual step under test for every other agent and for the Scorer.
6. Kill the Storybook background process you started (find its PID, e.g. via the job you backgrounded, or `lsof -i :6006` again, and `kill` it) so you don't leave a dangling server.
7. Run `git status --short` at the end and paste it. Expected: only the pre-existing 6 files for this step (overrides/app/hooks/useCartDrawer.ts modified→reverted so should show clean or match original diff baseline, useCartDrawer.test.tsx untracked, _app/index.tsx + index.test.tsx modified, product-view/index.tsx + index.test.tsx modified). Nothing else — no stray scratch files inside the repo, no leftover Storybook build artifacts committed to the tree (build-storybook output should not exist inside the repo; if `npm run storybook` in dev mode created any cache dirs under the repo like `.storybook-cache` or similar untracked noise, check whether they're gitignored — if not gitignored and newly appeared, flag it, don't delete build caches yourself without checking .gitignore first, but do report it).

## Also, separately (lighter effort): the base-precedent claim

The hook's docblock claims fixing a REAL pre-existing bug: `AddToCartModalProvider` was mounted in base `_app` but `<AddToCartModal />` was never rendered anywhere (base or override), so add-to-cart showed zero visual feedback. And that `CartDrawerProvider` (the new mechanism) fixes this by rendering `CartDrawerContainer` (which renders `<ZimmCartDrawer>`) in the exact same component body as the Provider, so the Provider can never be mounted without the real UI being fed real props. Sanity-check this structurally by reading `overrides/app/hooks/useCartDrawer.ts`'s `CartDrawerProvider` export (bottom of the file) — confirm it really does call `React.createElement(CartDrawerContainer, {...})` as a sibling to `children` inside the same `React.createElement(CartDrawerContext.Provider, ...)` call, not conditionally, not behind any flag. This one doesn't need Storybook — it's a direct code read. Report CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE either way.

## Report format

State plainly: (a) exact story IDs/URLs tested, (b) what you saw pre-mutation (all pass, or not), (c) what you saw post-mutation (crash confirmed, or not), (d) confirmation the file was reverted cleanly with `git diff` proof, (e) the CartDrawerProvider structural check, (f) final `git status --short` output. Label each as CONFIRMED (you personally observed it) — this whole angle is about direct observation, so PLAUSIBLE should be rare and only used if you genuinely could not get Storybook/Playwright working, in which case say exactly what you tried and where it broke down, per the "try, and report honestly if you can't" standard.
